items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Immeasurable Merit, and the Four Kinds of Utter Purity Explained in Full

items.zh: 三因緣故，說名無量。謂經於三無數大劫，無間修習乃圓證故，名時無量。於諸有情無量利益安樂意樂增上緣力所集成故，名為妙善意樂無量。無量善業差別品類所集成故，名品無量。故言無量福德資糧修習圓證，能起如來諸相、隨好。云何如來四一切種清淨？一者、一切種所依清淨，二者、一切種所緣清淨，三者、一切種心清淨，四者、一切種智清淨。云何一切種所依清淨？謂一切煩惱品麁重并諸習氣，於自所依無餘永滅；又於自體，如自所欲取住捨中自在而轉；是名一切種所依清淨。云何一切種所緣清淨？謂於種種若化、若變、若所顯現一切所緣皆自在轉，是名一切種所緣清淨。云何一切種心清淨？謂如前說一切心麁重永滅離故，又於心中一切種善根皆積集故，是名一切種心清淨。云何一切種智清淨？謂如前說一切無明品麁重永滅離故，又遍一切所知境中智無障礙、智自在轉，是名一切種智清淨。
items.en:
Third, concluding. Therefore it is said: immeasurable stores of merit, cultivated and fully realised, give rise to the Tathāgata's marks and exemplary signs.
Second, the four kinds of utter purity; first, posing the question. What are the Tathāgata's own four kinds of utter purity?
Second, listing them. First, purity of every basis; second, purity of every object; third, purity of every mind; fourth, purity of every wisdom.
Third, explaining; first, purity of every basis. What is purity of every basis? It means that every coarse affliction together with its habitual residue is permanently extinguished without remainder in one's own basis, and that with respect to one's own embodiment, one turns freely, exactly as one wishes, in taking it up, dwelling in it, or relinquishing it — this is called purity of every basis.
Second, purity of every object. What is purity of every object? It means that with respect to whatever is conjured, transformed, or manifested in various ways, one turns freely with respect to every such object — this is called purity of every object.
Third, purity of every mind. What is purity of every mind? It means, as said before, that every coarse affliction of the mind is permanently extinguished, and that every kind of wholesome root is gathered within the mind — this is called purity of every mind.
Fourth, purity of every wisdom. What is purity of every wisdom? It means, as said before, that every coarse form of ignorance is permanently extinguished, and that wisdom, throughout the entire range of all knowable objects, is unobstructed and turns freely — this is called purity of every wisdom.

items.title: Section: The Ten Powers Named, Why the Buddha Is Called "Thus Come," and the First Power's Ground in the Rightness of Cause and Effect

items.zh: 云何如來十力？一者、處非處智力，二者、自業智力，三者、靜慮解脫等持等至智力，四者、根勝劣智力，五者、種種勝解智力，六者、種種界智力，七者、遍趣行智力，八者、宿住隨念智力，九者、死生智力，十者、漏盡智力。如是十種如來智力，當知廣如十力經說。當知此中，諸有所言、所說、所宣，一切如實皆無虛妄，故名如來。淨不淨果非不平等，如實轉因，是名為處，亦名建立、亦名為依、亦名為起。淨不淨果不平等因，與上相違，是名非處。
items.en:
Third, the ten powers; first, posing the question. What are the Tathāgata's own ten powers?
Second, listing them. First, the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible; second, the power of wisdom regarding one's own karma; third, the power of wisdom regarding meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments; fourth, the power of wisdom regarding superior and inferior faculties; fifth, the power of wisdom regarding various resolute inclinations; sixth, the power of wisdom regarding various elements; seventh, the power of wisdom regarding the paths to every destination; eighth, the power of wisdom recollecting past abodes; ninth, the power of wisdom regarding death and rebirth; tenth, the power of wisdom regarding the exhaustion of outflows.
Third, pointing [to the source]. These ten powers of the Tathāgata's wisdom should be known in full detail as taught in the Sūtra of the Ten Powers.
Fourth, explaining; first, distinguishing individually; first, explaining the name "Tathāgata." Know that here, whatever is said, taught, and proclaimed is, in every case, exactly as it truly is, without any falsehood — hence the name "Tathāgata."
Second, explaining the ten powers themselves; first, the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible; first, distinguishing the names individually; first, distinguishing possible from impossible; first, possible. A pure or impure result not mismatched with its cause, the cause operating exactly as it truly is — this is called "possible," also called establishment, also called basis, also called arising.
Second, impossible. A pure or impure result ascribed to a cause that does not correspond to it, contrary to what was said above — this is called "impossible."

items.title: Section: What Makes This Wisdom "As It Truly Is," and Why It Is Called "Power" at All

items.zh: 遠離一切增上慢智，說名如實。若一切智、若無滯智、若清淨智，當知說名遠離一切增上慢智。如是一切智等諸句，當知如前最極無上菩提品說。數之次第最居其首，故名第一。以無上故，與一切種饒益一切有情功能具相應故，畢竟勝伏一切魔怨大威力故，說名為力。
items.en:
Second, explaining the nature of wisdom-power; first, wisdom; first, stating [that it is] as it truly is. Wisdom entirely free of every over-estimation is called "as it truly is."
Second, explaining freedom from over-estimation. Possessing all-wisdom, unimpeded wisdom, and pure wisdom — know that this is called freedom from every over-estimation.
Second, power. Because it is unsurpassed, because it is endowed with the capacity to benefit all beings in every way, and because it possesses the great might to utterly subdue every demonic adversary, it is called "power."

items.title: Section: Five Names for the First Power — Great Nirvāṇa, Sage-Lordship, Self-Knowing, Turning the Brahma-Wheel, and the Lion's Roar

items.zh: 攝受如實圓證因故，如其所欲皆能現行自在轉故，說名成就最上涅槃。以無上故，說名為大。八支聖道所證得故，遠離一切災患畏故，名仙尊位。能自了知自所證故，說名自知。既自證已，由哀愍心，廣為有情等開示故，名轉梵輪。何以故？謂諸如來有是增語，說名為梵，名為寂靜，亦名清涼。最初能轉，從此已後餘復為餘，如是展轉梵所推運，周旋一切有情眾中，故名梵輪。自顯墮在最上施設無上大師圓滿攝故；能說彼道對治一切餘邪道故；於道怨敵異論現前無怯弱故；為欲勝伏一切他論，宣揚廣大無上論故；名大眾中正師子吼。
items.en:
Second, showing the overall meaning; first, explaining the [five] qualities; first, called great nirvāṇa. Because he has gathered in the cause for perfectly realising [wisdom] exactly as it truly is, and because he can freely manifest whatever he wishes, this is called attaining the supreme nirvāṇa; because it is unsurpassed, it is called "great."
Second, called the position of the sage-lord. Because it is attained through the eightfold noble path and brings freedom from every calamity and fear, it is called the position of the sage-lord.
Third, called self-knowing. Because he can clearly know for himself what he has realised, it is called self-knowing.
Fourth, called turning the brahma-wheel. Having realised it himself, moved by compassion, he broadly reveals it to beings; this is called turning the brahma-wheel. Why? Because the Tathāgatas have this epithet: it is called "brahma," also called "tranquil," also called "cooling." Being first to turn it, with others thereafter turning it in succession, it is thus turned onward by "brahma," circulating throughout every assembly of beings; hence it is called the brahma-wheel.
Fifth, called the lion's roar. Because he reveals himself as belonging to the supreme, complete great teacher; because he can teach the path that counters every other mistaken path; because he shows no timidity when confronted by hostile, contrary views; and because he seeks to overcome every rival doctrine by proclaiming the vast, unsurpassed teaching — it is called correctly roaring the lion's roar amid the great assembly.

items.zh: 以要言之，當知此中顯發、辯了、施設、開示自利行滿，利他行滿，自利利他圓滿不共。

items.title: Section: A Physician's Own Simile Closes the First Power — Cured, Able to Cure, and Silencing Every False Physician

items.zh: 復有異門。此中略義，謂所應得得勝方便。此勝方便，一切眾會隨所樂欲，或天或人一切皆從我所獲得此勝方便。如病除愈，當知此顯自知已得大安隱處。如彼疾病除愈方便，當知此顯轉於梵輪。如遮一切邪醫，自稱顯已決定能愈眾疾，當知此顯於大眾中正師子吼。
items.en:
Second, a further way of stating [the point]. There is also another way of expressing this. In brief, this means the supreme means one should attain. This supreme means — every assembly, whatever they wish, whether in the heavens or the human realm, all obtain this supreme means from me alone. Just as a sick person is cured [by a physician], know this illustrates self-knowing that one has attained the great, secure ground. Just as that means of curing illness [is what is needed], know this illustrates turning the brahma-wheel. Just as one who refutes every false physician declares himself certain to cure every affliction, know this illustrates correctly roaring the lion's roar amid the great assembly.
The power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible should be known as the wisdom accomplished through thoroughly understanding the truth of dependent origination.

blocks.text: The four purities found only in a buddha, and then the ten powers, beginning with the knowledge of what is and is not possible.

subs.head: Mastery over the body and world

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: an ordinary person's karmic result doesn't follow one's wishes. Master Cháng Bǎi: we cannot even know whether tomorrow or the next life comes first. And on transforming things: ordinary people cling to the elements as real, and so meet obstruction everywhere.

"Whatever is said, taught, and proclaimed is true": sūtra, vinaya, and treatise, as both teachers read it. On the first power: Master Cháng Bǎi, outsiders attribute good and bad results to Maheśvara, a mismatched cause.
Venerable Miào Jìng: lacking wisdom yet thinking one has it; unaware of the error, one isn't lying. Master Cháng Bǎi: a mistaken understanding, sometimes adding, sometimes subtracting.
"The Tathāgatas have this epithet: it is called brahma, also tranquil, also cooling." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is an honorific of the Buddha, passed on by disciple after disciple.

Cured oneself is self-knowing; the method of cure is the wheel; refuting false doctors is the lion's roar. Master Cháng Bǎi: the true doctor stops all false ones. Venerable Miào Jìng: declaring "I am a good doctor".
The physician simile is old and central: the Buddha as the doctor, the Dharma as the medicine. Here it explains the lion's roar: not boasting, but the confidence of one who has been cured.

quiz.q: Purity of basis: "turning freely in taking up, dwelling, and relinquishing." How do the lectures contrast the Buddha and ordinary people?
options: the Buddha is free; our karma doesn't follow our wishes — we don't know whether tomorrow or the next life comes first
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: an ordinary person's karmic result doesn't follow one's wishes. Master Cháng Bǎi: we cannot even know whether tomorrow or the next life comes first.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain "conjured" and "transformed" in purity of object?
options: Miào Jìng: altering what exists is 變; Cháng Bǎi: mountains into seas, while ordinary people cling to the elements as real
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: altering what already exists is 變. Master Cháng Bǎi: mountains into seas; ordinary people cling to the elements as real, and so meet obstruction everywhere.

quiz.q: How is the name "Tathāgata" explained here?
options: whatever is said, taught, and proclaimed is true, without falsehood
quiz.why: Whatever is said, taught, and proclaimed is true — sūtra, vinaya, and treatise, as both teachers read it.

quiz.q: "Unequal cause" is rendered "disproportionate cause." What examples do the lectures give?
options: outsiders attributing results to Maheśvara or Brahmā — a false cause, not a matter of proportion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders attribute good and bad results to Maheśvara — an unequal cause. Venerable Miào Jìng cites the view that Brahmā causes one's suffering. "Disproportionate" suggests size; the lectures mean a mismatched cause.

quiz.q: "Wisdom free of over-estimation." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain over-estimation?
options: thinking one has wisdom when one doesn't — unaware of the error, so not a lie
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: lacking wisdom yet thinking one has it; unaware of the error, one isn't lying. Master Cháng Bǎi: a mistaken understanding, sometimes adding, sometimes subtracting.

options: an epithet of the Tathāgatas, also "tranquil" and "cooling"
quiz.why: "The Tathāgatas have this epithet: it is called brahma, also tranquil, also cooling." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is an honorific of the Buddha, passed on by disciple after disciple.

quiz.q: The second reading uses a medical simile. How do its parts match, and what do the lectures say?
options: cure = self-knowing, method = wheel, refuting false doctors = lion's roar; both lectures so read it
quiz.why: Cure is self-knowing; the method is the wheel; refuting false doctors is the lion's roar. Master Cháng Bǎi: the true doctor stops all false ones. Venerable Miào Jìng: declaring "I am a good doctor."
